study.title: Yin-Yang Harmony Acupuncture Therapy improves facial motor function and resting state facial appearance in peripheral facial paralysis
study.population: Patients diagnosed with peripheral facial paralysis at the Affiliated Hospital of Jiangnan University between January 2018 and January 2024
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) diagnosis of peripheral facial paralysis according to the Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Peripheral Facial Paralysis with Integrated Chinese and Western Medicine; (2) age ≥ 18 years; (3) receipt of either standard acupuncture treatment or Yin-Yang harmonizing acupuncture; (4) disease duration ≤ 2 weeks; (5) unilateral facial paralysis; (6) complete clinical records and comprehensive case information; and (7) completion of a three-month follow-up
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) confirmed diagnosis of malignancy; (2) presence of neuropsychiatric disorders or cognitive impairment; (3) refractory peripheral facial paralysis secondary to conditions such as craniocerebral injury; (4) pregnancy or lactation; (5) hemorrhagic disorders, such as hemophilia or coagulation dysfunction; or (6) severe cardiovascular or cerebrovascular diseases

interventions.procedure_label_exact: Western medical treatment (base regimen for conventional acupuncture group)
interventions.treatment_period_exact: Two weeks (medications); five days then taper (prednisone)

interventions.anatomical_location_exact: Local acupoints on the affected side; distal acupoints bilaterally
interventions.laterality_exact: Local acupoints on affected side; Hegu and Zusanli bilaterally
interventions.depth_exact: Yangbai: 0.5-1 inch; Fengchi: 0.3-1.1 inches; Xiaguan and Yifeng: 1.5 inches; Sibai: 0.2-0.3 inches; Jiache: 2-3 inches; Cuanzhu: 0.3-0.5 inches; Dicang: 1.5-2.5 inches; Hegu: 0.3-0.5 inches; Zusanli: 0.6-1.2 inches
interventions.manipulation_exact: Yangbai: needled perpendicularly along the frontal plane at an angle of approximately 10°; Fengchi: needled from the posterior aspect, directed inward and downward towards the philtrum or nasal tip at a 45° angle relative to the sagittal plane; Xiaguan and Yifeng: needled perpendicularly and slightly downward; Sibai: needled obliquely upward; Jiache: needled from the posterior aspect towards the mouth corner; Cuanzhu: obliquely needled downward through Jingming; Dicang: needled through to Jiache; Hegu: needled obliquely toward the second metacarpal bone at an 80° angle relative to the dorsum of the hand; Zusanli: needled horizontally at a 90° angle to the lateral aspect of the lower leg
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: 10 sessions per course; once every two days
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Standard acupuncture treatment for peripheral facial paralysis

interventions.procedure_label_exact: Western medical treatment (base regimen for YYHAT group)
interventions.treatment_period_exact: Two weeks (medications); five days then taper (prednisone)

interventions.stimulation_type: manual acupuncture with needle retention and moxibustion
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: Local acupoints on the affected side; distal acupoints bilaterally; two additional acupoints (Shuigou and Chengjiang) on the affected side
interventions.laterality_exact: Local acupoints and additional acupoints on affected side; Hegu and Zusanli bilaterally
interventions.depth_exact: Shuigou: 0.2-0.3 inches; Chengjiang: 0.3-0.5 inches; (same as conventional for all other acupoints)
interventions.manipulation_exact: Shuigou: needled either obliquely upward or perpendicularly, followed by moxibustion with 3-5 moxa cones; Chengjiang: needled obliquely, subsequently treated with mild moxibustion for 5-10 minutes; all other acupoints same as conventional group
interventions.number_of_sessions_exact: once every two days, for a total of 10 sessions per course, consistent with the conventional acupuncture group
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Yin-Yang Harmony Acupuncture Therapy is a refined acupuncture approach grounded in the principles of TCM, specifically the dynamic balance between Yin and Yang; aims to restore systemic equilibrium and promote both local and global physiological regulation by selecting specific acupoints based on individualized syndrome differentiation

sensory_interoceptive_responses.notes: Sensory/interoceptive responses (e.g., deqi) were not measured or reported in this study

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: Acuson S2000, Siemens, Germany (color Doppler ultrasound); KEYPOINT, Guangzhou Weidi Medical Equipment Co., Ltd., China (electromyographic evoked potential instrument)

extraction_notes.note: This study does not include functional brain neuroimaging (fMRI, PET, EEG, etc.). The neuroimaging methods section captures sEMG and Doppler ultrasound, which are physiological/electrophysiological measures of peripheral nerve and vascular function, not central nervous system neuroimaging. The study is not a brain neuroimaging study.
Sensory/interoceptive responses (deqi sensations) during acupuncture were not measured or reported in this study. No deqi scale, MASS, or comparable instrument was administered.
Expectancy, blinding success, credibility, and allocation guessing were not assessed or reported.
Adverse events were not reported in this study.
Trial registration number was not reported.
The study is retrospective, not randomized. No randomization procedure is described. Groups were determined by treatment modality received, not by random allocation.

Exact numeric mean ± SD values for sEMG latency and amplitude before and after treatment are reported only in figures (Figures 1 and 2) and cannot be precisely read from the PDF. Only p-values and directional conclusions are available from the text. Values in figures are approximations from bar charts.

The paper states modified House-Brackmann (H-B) scores and Facial Disability Index Scores (FDIS) were collected in the data collection section, but no results for these measures are presented in the results section. These outcomes appear to have been collected but not reported.

The treatment period for the acupuncture courses (10 sessions over how many total weeks) is not explicitly stated beyond 'once every two days, for a total of 10 sessions per course'. Total duration of acupuncture treatment is not precisely stated.

The paper states both groups received a three-month follow-up (inclusion criterion 7), but no three-month follow-up outcome data are reported in the results. All reported outcomes appear to be at three weeks post-treatment.

The paper classifies YYHAT as using moxibustion (at Shuigou and Chengjiang) in addition to manual acupuncture needling. The acupuncture_modality field is set to manual_acupuncture as the primary modality, but the intervention also includes moxibustion. The combined nature is noted in manipulation_exact.
Data availability statement was not provided.

The therapeutic efficacy categories label both 'effective' (total score 14-16) and 'effective' (total score < 14) appear to have the same label in the paper text, with the < 14 category likely being 'ineffective'. The results table correctly labels this as 'Ineffective', suggesting a typographic error in the methods text.
